audit_questions.normal_exit_persisting_running: YES — observed in all four scenarios. Within the live production service this is designed P4B semantics (runs persist across invocations; recovery is the restart terminalizer, spec §15.6). In a ONE-SHOT driver (the benchmark CLI) the process exits normally and the row persists 'running' indefinitely unless a later service startup sweeps it or the store is deleted.
audit_questions.who_terminalizes_after_plan_containment: NOBODY in the one-shot path. PLAN containment (exception / v2-resolution rejection / validator rejection) deliberately does NOT terminalize — unlike INTEGRATE containment which calls fail_run(internal_failure). The only terminalizer is AgentRuntimeRepository.recover_interrupted_agent_runtime(), invoked at the NEXT orchestrator.initialize() (service startup), which the one-shot CLI never reaches.
audit_questions.run_loop_final_cleanup: run_loop has no exit cleanup — consistent with its live-service design (it must NOT terminalize: the next invocation continues the run). The gap is at the DRIVER exit boundary, not in run_loop.
audit_questions.restart_recovery_role: VERIFIED correct and exclusively abnormal-exit-oriented: queued/running runs -> failed(runtime_restart), queued/running delegations -> failed, active investigations -> paused(runtime_restart); idempotent (second call zeros); does not re-execute or resume; 4/4 scenarios terminalized.
audit_questions.cancellederror_and_task_deletion: CancelledError is NEVER converted to an ordinary failure (except Exception only, verified live: zero diagnostics entries, zero containment events, CLI crash with raw CancelledError). Task deletion removes the store including any stale row (no zombie rows; the driver's --cleanup-tasks path deletes through the normal lifecycle API).
audit_questions.status_write_failure_fail_closed: YES — every run transition is a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction (transition validation + trajectory append + commit); a failed write raises and rolls back with no half-state. In the PLAN containment path a trajectory-write failure propagates as an exception (cycle outcome lost) but never commits partial state: fail-closed, no fail-open.

cf1_verdict_scope: CF-1.1 (defect, confirmed): at the ONE-SHOT INVOCATION EXIT boundary there is no deterministic terminalizer for non-terminal AgentRun rows. A normally-ended, fully-successful benchmark execution persists 'running' (observed in the control scenario); a PLAN-contained failure persists 'running' (observed in invalid-union and timeout scenarios). The durable state contradicts the execution reality for the lifetime of the store unless an out-of-band recovery sweep runs.

CF-1.2 (inconsistency, confirmed; designed for the live service): PLAN containment is non-terminal while INTEGRATE containment is terminal (fail_run). The asymmetry is intentional (PLAN rejection must stay retryable so a live service can re-plan on the next invocation) but is recorded nowhere in the lifecycle contract/spec, and it yields asymmetric durable records for equivalent contained-model-failure causes in one-shot artifacts.

CF-1.3 (explicitly NOT defects): CancelledError pass-through; recovery sweep correctness/idempotence/no-re-execution; FinalizationGate fail-closed denial (no record, no run transition); typed timeout classification; transactional status writes.

option_A_driver_side_settle_reusing_the_.change: The one-shot driver (run_p8b_baseline / ProductionBenchmarkExecutor.execute) invokes the EXISTING AgentRuntimeRepository.recover_interrupted_agent_runtime() once after run_loop + finalization and BEFORE persisting the snapshot. Nothing else changes.
option_A_driver_side_settle_reusing_the_.rationale: At driver exit the runtime genuinely stops; the recovery primitive is the frozen, idempotent, spec-§15.6 terminalizer; the persisted snapshot then records the terminal row while the containment cause stays preserved in trajectory + diagnostics. Zero schema change, zero orchestrator behavior change, zero live-service impact.
option_A_driver_side_settle_reusing_the_.rejected_variant: a narrower driver-side fail_run(budget_exhausted) — rejected: misstates the cause; a new RunStopReason member would be a frozen-enum change.
option_A_driver_side_settle_reusing_the_.authorization: Runtime-affecting change — NOT IMPLEMENTED in RCA-2A.2c; requires independent authorization.

option_B_first_class_invocation_exit_sto.change: new RunStopReason member (e.g. invocation_exit) + an orchestrator terminalization method invoked when the caller declares it will not re-invoke.
option_B_first_class_invocation_exit_sto.cost: touches the frozen RunStopReason enum + RUN_TRANSITIONS + spec §15.2; honest semantics but a runtime contract change.
option_B_first_class_invocation_exit_sto.authorization: requires independent authorization; recorded as the alternative.

minimal_fix_design_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.option_C_rejected: making PLAN containment itself terminal — REJECTED by this audit: it would regress live-service re-plan semantics (a transient provider failure must not kill the run). Any fix must preserve non-terminal PLAN containment in the live service.

regression_test_design_for_the_fix_NOT_I: driver-exit settle: after execute_cycle + finalize denial, the settle call terminalizes the row (failed/runtime_restart); the snapshot records a terminal run; containment cause remains in trajectory + diagnostics; second call is a no-op (idempotent).
live-service non-regression: PLAN containment followed by a NEW execute_cycle invocation re-plans successfully in the SAME run — proving the fix did not make PLAN containment terminal.
both are expressible as extensions of tests/unit/investigation/test_rca2a2c_plan_lifecycle_contract.py
